rows.note: Use 羞恥心 for the inner feeling of shame and for a person's sense of decency; it is the all-purpose noun for these meanings.

example.english: They have no sense of shame even when they do something wrong.
example.jyutping: keoi5 zou6 co3 si6 dou1 mou5 sau1 ci2 sam1

rows.note: Use 遺憾 when “a shame” means something regrettable or disappointing rather than moral shame.

example.english: It’s a real shame that this trip was cancelled because of the rain.
example.traditional: 今次旅行因為落雨取消，真係遺憾。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 leoi5 hang4 jan1 wai6 lok6 jyu5 ceoi2 siu1 zan1 hai6 wai4 ham6

rows.note: Use 恥辱 for public dishonour or disgrace, rather than the personal feeling expressed by 羞恥心.

example.english: This defeat was a great shame for the whole team.
example.traditional: 呢場敗仗對全隊嚟講係一大恥辱。
example.jyutping: ni1 coeng4 baai6 zoeng3 deoi3 cyun4 deoi2 lei4 gong2 hai6 jat1 daai6 ci2 juk6

rows.note: Use 私處 specifically for the private parts when “shame” refers to the body rather than to modesty or emotion.

example.english: The doctor said there was no need to feel shame about problems with your private parts.
example.traditional: 醫生話私處有問題，唔使覺得羞恥。
example.jyutping: ji1 sang1 waa6 si1 cyu3 jau5 man6 tai4 m4 sai2 gok3 dak1 sau1 ci2
